stemMd: Which feature distinguishes a perspective view of a long corridor from a parallel axonometric view of the same corridor?

options.label: A
options.textMd: All objects retain equal image size regardless of distance

options.label: C
options.textMd: Straight walls become curved in every perspective view

options.label: D
options.textMd: The corridor must be drawn without a floor

options.label: E
options.textMd: Parallel receding edges may converge toward a vanishing point

explanationMd: In linear perspective, rays pass through a finite viewpoint. Parallel lines not parallel to the image plane approach a common vanishing point. In a parallel axonometric view, corresponding parallel directions remain parallel.

distractorRationale.b: Perspective can show vertical edges normally.
distractorRationale.a: That is characteristic of parallel projection, not perspective.
distractorRationale.c: Ordinary linear perspective preserves straight lines.
distractorRationale.d: Floor visibility is unrelated to projection type.
